purpose: Make the Legacy publish-boundary state and truth timing behavior executable without linking Legacy into product or reference probes.

provenance.notes: The Python comparator verifies the frozen archive, three raw source entries, the recorded passing Legacy CTest and the exact input bytes. Decimal analysis and the isolated C++17 probe independently exercise both publish boundaries.

expected_facts.claim: Publishing t_k projects the committed state without changing its altitude or vertical velocity.
expected_facts.tolerance_policy: Committed-state values before and after each publish are exactly identical.

expected_facts.claim: Truth uses the committed state and current boundary time when published, then retains that sample until the next publish boundary.
expected_facts.tolerance_policy: Sample time and event order are exact; synthetic trajectory values use absolute tolerance 1e-12.

expected_facts.claim: The observation is tied to the frozen Legacy archive, simulator, PointMass and test entries, and a passing recorded runtime test.
expected_facts.tolerance_policy: Paths, byte counts and SHA-256 values are exact.

acceptance: Verifies frozen source and runtime-test evidence before comparing behavior
Independent Decimal and C++17 implementations agree on both publish boundaries and the analytic t1 state
